--- title: "English's grammatical features are less widely shared than those of most languages studied" subtitle: "English's grammatical features in Grambank average a family share of 42%, against 46% for the median of the 1,320 plotted languages." description: "English's 63 recorded grammatical features average a family share of 42%, below the 46% median of 1,320 languages in Grambank. Each feature is weighted so every language family counts equally, and each language is placed at the average of its own features on a shared scale. Built in R with ggplot2, ggbeeswarm, patchwork and ggtext." date: "2026-11-02" author: - name: "Steven Ponce" url: "https://stevenponce.netlify.app" citation: url: "https://stevenponce.netlify.app/data_visualizations/TidyTuesday/2026/tt_2026_44.html" categories: ["TidyTuesday", "2026"] tags: [ "TidyTuesday", "Grambank", "Linguistics", "Language Typology", "Grammar", "English", "Beeswarm", "Distribution", "Family-Weighted Prevalence", "Small Multiples", "ggbeeswarm", "patchwork", "ggtext", "2026" ] image: "thumbnails/tt_2026_44.png" format: html: toc: true toc-depth: 5 code-link: true code-fold: true code-tools: true code-summary: "Show code" editor_options: chunk_output_type: inline execute: freeze: true cache: true error: false message: false warning: false eval: true --- ![Two-panel beeswarm chart titled "English's grammatical features are less widely shared than those of most languages studied." English's features average a family share of 42% (the share of languages with a feature, each language family weighted equally), against 46% for the median of 1,320 plotted languages. Panel A places English's 63 grammatical features on a 0–100% family-share axis, with a burgundy tick marking English's average. Four rare features are highlighted in burgundy: word order can mark a question ("Is it raining?", 2%), a free passive auxiliary ("was sold", 5%), an indefinite article ("a dog", 9%), and one past form for every person ("I/she walked", 9%). Two common controls appear for contrast: past tense on the verb (62%) and a verb suffix (93%). Panel B plots each language at the average family share of its own features; they form a narrow cloud between about 35% and 58%, with English on the left. Source: Grambank v1.0.3 via TidyTuesday.](tt_2026_44.png){#fig-1} ### [**Steps to Create this Graphic**]{.mark} #### [1. Load Packages & Setup]{.smallcaps} ::: {.cell} ````{.cell-code} ```{{r}} #| label: load #| warning: false #| message: false #| results: "hide" ## 1. LOAD PACKAGES & SETUP ---- suppressPackageStartupMessages({ if (!require("pacman")) install.packages("pacman") pacman::p_load( tidyverse, ggtext, showtext, scales, glue, ggview, ggbeeswarm, patchwork, ragg ) }) # Source utility functions suppressMessages(source(here::here("R/utils/fonts.R"))) source(here::here("R/utils/social_icons.R")) source(here::here("R/utils/image_utils.R")) source(here::here("R/themes/base_theme.R")) ``` ```` ::: #### [2. Read in the Data]{.smallcaps} ::: {.cell} ````{.cell-code} ```{{r}} #| label: read #| include: true #| eval: true #| warning: false ### |- figure settings ---- fig_w <- 10 fig_h <- 9 fig_dpi <- 320 ### |- fonts ---- setup_fonts() fonts <- get_font_families() title_family <- fonts$title_1 ## 2. READ IN THE DATA ---- ## Read every field as character with no NA tokens: Grambank writes isolates' family as ## the literal "NA", and tt_load() cannot be told otherwise. tt_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2026/2026-11-03/" read_chr <- function(url) { read_csv(url, col_types = cols(.default = col_character()), na = character(), show_col_types = FALSE) } languages_raw <- read_chr(paste0(tt_url, "grambank_languages.csv")) parameters_raw <- read_chr(paste0(tt_url, "grambank_parameters.csv")) values_raw <- read_chr(paste0(tt_url, "grambank_values.csv")) # Grambank's own languages table (v1.0.3, same release as the TT extract): variety level and # language-level ID, which the TT extract drops gb_languages_raw <- read_chr("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/grambank/grambank/v1.0.3/cldf/languages.csv") ``` ```` ::: #### [3. Examine the Data]{.smallcaps} ::: {.cell} ````{.cell-code} ```{{r}} #| label: examine #| include: true #| eval: true #| results: 'hide' #| warning: false ## 3. EXAMINING THE DATA ---- glimpse(languages_raw) glimpse(parameters_raw) glimpse(values_raw) ``` ```` ::: #### [4. Tidy Data]{.smallcaps} ::: {.cell} ````{.cell-code} ```{{r}} #| label: tidy #| warning: false ### |- analysis frame: one variety per language, no proto-languages ---- multistate_ids <- c("GB024", "GB025", "GB065", "GB130", "GB193", "GB203") coded_counts <- values_raw |> count(language_id, name = "n_coded") analysis_ids <- gb_languages_raw |> filter(level != "family") |> left_join(coded_counts, by = c("ID" = "language_id")) |> slice_max(n_coded, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE, by = Language_level_ID) |> pull(ID) languages <- languages_raw |> filter(language_id %in% analysis_ids) |> mutate(family_unit = if_else(family_name == "NA", paste0("isolate_", language_id), family_name)) binary_values <- values_raw |> filter(!parameter_id %in% multistate_ids, language_id %in% analysis_ids) |> mutate(present = as.integer(value)) |> left_join(languages |> select(language_id, family_unit), by = "language_id") ### |- family-balanced share for each feature ---- ## within each family: share of its recorded languages with the feature; ## then the mean over families with a recorded answer (each isolate is one family) feature_share <- binary_values |> summarise(family_rate = mean(present), .by = c(parameter_id, family_unit)) |> summarise(family_share = mean(family_rate), n_families = n(), .by = parameter_id) ### |- English's present features (panel A) ---- english_id <- "stan1293" english_features <- binary_values |> filter(language_id == english_id, present == 1) |> left_join(feature_share, by = "parameter_id") ### |- each language's average (panel B) ---- min_recorded <- 150 language_avg <- binary_values |> left_join(feature_share, by = "parameter_id") |> summarise(n_recorded = n(), avg_share = mean(family_share[present == 1]), .by = language_id) |> filter(n_recorded >= min_recorded) english_avg <- language_avg$avg_share[language_avg$language_id == english_id] median_avg <- median(language_avg$avg_share) share_more_common <- mean(language_avg$avg_share > english_avg) ### |- named features: four rarest English features + two widely shared controls ---- named_features <- tribble( ~parameter_id, ~example, ~device, ~side, "GB260", "Is it raining?", "word order can mark a question", "rare", "GB302", "was sold", "free passive auxiliary", "rare", "GB021", "a dog", "indefinite article", "rare", "GB400", "I / she walked", "one past form for every person", "rare", "GB083", "walk-ed", "past tense on the verb", "control", "GB080", "bark-ing", "suffix on the verb", "control" ) ``` ```` ::: #### [5. Visualization Parameters]{.smallcaps} ::: {.cell} ````{.cell-code} ```{{r}} #| label: params #| include: true #| warning: false ### |- plot aesthetics ---- clrs <- get_theme_colors( palette = list( accent = "#722F37", ink = "#2C2825", dot = "#8A8178", cloud = "#C9C1B6", ref = "#D9D3C9", muted = "#7A7068" ) ) col_accent <- clrs$palette$accent col_ink <- clrs$palette$ink col_dot <- clrs$palette$dot col_cloud <- clrs$palette$cloud col_ref <- clrs$palette$ref col_muted <- clrs$palette$muted ### |- titles and caption ---- title_text <- "English's grammatical features are less widely shared\nthan those of most languages studied" subtitle_text <- glue( "**English**'s grammatical features in Grambank average a family share of ", "**{round(100 * english_avg)}%**, against **{round(100 * median_avg)}%** for the
median of the {comma(nrow(language_avg))} plotted languages." ) cue_a <- "Each dot is one feature, placed by its family share: the share of languages with it, each language family weighted equally" caption_lines <- c( "Family share: within each language family, the share of its recorded languages with the feature, averaged over families with a recorded answer.", glue( "Isolates count as one family each; multi-value word-order features and '?' answers excluded. ", "Panel B: languages with {min_recorded}+ of 189 features recorded." ) ) disclosure_text <- glue( "{caption_lines[1]}
{caption_lines[2]}" ) caption_text <- paste0( disclosure_text, "
", create_social_caption( tt_year = 2026, tt_week = 44, source_text = "Grambank v1.0.3 (Skirgård et al. 2023) via TidyTuesday, curated by Ntobeko Sosibo" ) ) ### |- plot theme ---- base_theme <- create_base_theme(clrs) weekly_theme <- extend_weekly_theme( base_theme, theme( plot.title = element_text( face = "bold", family = title_family, size = 26, color = col_ink, lineheight = 1.0, margin = margin(b = 10) ), plot.subtitle = element_markdown( family = fonts$subtitle, size = 12, color = col_ink, lineheight = 1.25, margin = margin(b = 6) ), plot.caption = element_markdown( family = fonts$caption, size = 6.8, color = col_muted, hjust = 0, lineheight = 1.35, margin = margin(t = 12) ), axis.text.x = element_text(family = fonts$text, size = 9, color = col_muted), axis.title.x = element_text( family = fonts$text, size = 9, color = col_muted, face = "plain", margin = margin(t = 6) ), axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.title.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank(), panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = "none", plot.margin = margin(14, 24, 8, 20) ) ) theme_set(weekly_theme) ### |- shared x scale ---- x_scale <- scale_x_continuous( limits = c(0, 1), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25), labels = label_percent(), expand = expansion(add = c(0.01, 0.01)) ) ``` ```` ::: #### [6. Plot]{.smallcaps} ::: {.cell} ````{.cell-code} ```{{r}} #| label: plot #| warning: false ### |- panel A: English's 63 features ---- set.seed(2026) swarm_a <- layer_data( ggplot(english_features, aes(family_share, 0)) + geom_quasirandom(orientation = "y", width = 0.32, method = "pseudorandom", ) ) |> select(x, y) |> bind_cols(english_features |> select(parameter_id, family_share)) labels_a <- named_features |> left_join(swarm_a, by = "parameter_id") |> mutate( pct = round(100 * family_share), label = glue("{example} · {device} · {pct}%"), label_y = c(0.92, -0.88, 0.66, -0.52, 0.80, -0.80), hjust = case_when(parameter_id == "GB080" ~ 1, TRUE ~ 0), colour = if_else(side == "rare", col_accent, col_ink) ) p_a <- ggplot(swarm_a, aes(x, y)) + annotate("segment", x = 0.5, xend = 0.5, y = -1.2, yend = 1.08, color = col_ref, linewidth = 0.35) + annotate("text", x = 0.505, y = 1.06, label = "50% reference", family = fonts$text, size = 2.7, color = col_muted, hjust = 0 ) + geom_segment( data = labels_a, aes(x = x, xend = x, y = y, yend = label_y), color = col_ref, linewidth = 0.3 ) + geom_point(aes(color = family_share < 0.10), size = 2, stroke = 0) + geom_richtext( data = labels_a, aes(x = x, y = label_y, label = label, hjust = hjust), color = labels_a$colour, family = fonts$text, size = 3, fill = NA, label.colour = NA, label.padding = unit(c(1, 2, 1, 2), "pt"), vjust = if_else(labels_a$label_y > 0, 0, 1) ) + annotate("segment", x = english_avg, xend = english_avg, y = -1.20, yend = -0.96, color = col_accent, linewidth = 1.3, lineend = "butt" ) + annotate("text", x = english_avg - 0.006, y = -1.08, label = "English's average", family = fonts$text, size = 3.1, color = col_accent, fontface = "bold", hjust = 1 ) + annotate("text", x = 0, y = 1.42, hjust = 0, vjust = 1, family = fonts$text, size = 3.3, color = col_ink, fontface = "bold", label = "A The 63 grammatical features English has" ) + annotate("text", x = 0, y = 1.29, hjust = 0, vjust = 1, family = fonts$text, size = 2.9, color = col_muted, label = cue_a ) + scale_color_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = col_accent, `FALSE` = col_dot)) + x_scale + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-1.2, 1.45), expand = expansion(0)) + labs( title = title_text, subtitle = subtitle_text, x = "Family share of each feature (each family weighted equally)" ) ### |- panel B: 1,320 languages at their averages ---- set.seed(2026) swarm_b <- layer_data( ggplot(language_avg, aes(avg_share, 0)) + geom_quasirandom(orientation = "y", width = 0.42, method = "pseudorandom") ) |> select(x, y) p_b <- ggplot(language_avg, aes(avg_share, 0)) + annotate("segment", x = 0.5, xend = 0.5, y = -0.6, yend = 0.40, color = col_ref, linewidth = 0.35) + geom_quasirandom( orientation = "y", width = 0.42, method = "pseudorandom", size = 0.6, stroke = 0, color = col_cloud ) + annotate("segment", x = median_avg, xend = median_avg, y = -0.6, yend = 0.42, color = col_muted, linewidth = 0.35) + annotate("text", x = median_avg + 0.008, y = 0.5, label = "median of plotted languages", family = fonts$text, size = 2.8, color = col_muted, hjust = 0 ) + annotate("point", x = english_avg, y = 0, color = col_accent, size = 2.8) + annotate("segment", x = english_avg, xend = english_avg, y = 0.06, yend = 0.42, color = col_accent, linewidth = 0.3 ) + annotate("text", x = english_avg - 0.008, y = 0.5, label = "English", family = fonts$text, size = 3, color = col_accent, fontface = "bold", hjust = 1 ) + annotate("text", x = 0, y = 0.98, hjust = 0, vjust = 1, family = fonts$text, size = 3.3, color = col_ink, fontface = "bold", label = glue("B English among {comma(nrow(language_avg))} languages") ) + annotate("text", x = 0, y = 0.85, hjust = 0, vjust = 1, family = fonts$text, size = 2.9, color = col_muted, label = "Each dot is one language, placed at the average position of its own features" ) + x_scale + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-0.6, 1.0), expand = expansion(0)) + labs( x = "Average family share across the language's own features", caption = caption_text ) ### |- combine ---- p <- p_a / p_b + plot_layout(heights = c(1.45, 1)) ``` ```` ::: ### [7. Save]{.smallcaps} ::: {.cell} ````{.cell-code} ```{{r}} #| label: save #| warning: false ### |- save ---- main_path <- here::here("data_visualizations", "TidyTuesday", "2026", "tt_2026_44.png") thumb_path <- here::here("data_visualizations", "TidyTuesday", "2026", "thumbnails", "tt_2026_44.png") # Full-size version, for the QMD figure ggview::save_ggplot(plot = p, file = main_path, width = fig_w, height = fig_h, units = "in", dpi = fig_dpi) # Reduced-size thumbnail, for the YAML `image:` field fs::dir_create(dirname(thumb_path)) magick::image_read(main_path) |> magick::image_resize("400") |> magick::image_write(thumb_path) ``` ```` ::: #### [8.
